text:
Recent work supports separating latent interests and their temporal dynamics. [HyperHawkes (WWW 2025)](https://evazangerle.at/publication/peintner-www-2025/) discovers intents through contrastive clustering, models recurring intent with Hawkes processes, and combines this with short-term attention mixtures; intent labels are unnecessary. [IMA/EMA (TKDE 2024)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10400839/) retains existing intents, detects new ones, and removes inactive intents under memory constraints, although its focus is incremental adaptation rather than per-interaction switching. These approaches provide mechanisms for retaining interests that temporarily disappear.

For efficient temporal modeling, [Mamba4Rec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.03900) uses input-dependent selective state updates; this supplies an efficient backbone but does not itself establish multiple competing intent states. [SEMamba (2026)](https://academic.oup.com/comjnl/advance-article-abstract/doi/10.1093/comjnl/bxag107/8825404) combines global Mamba representations with gated local features for short-term shifts. [MaTra4LS (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2026.123445) similarly separates long-term Mamba and dynamic-window short-term Transformer branches, using low-rank fusion.

Research opportunity inferred from these results: maintain several recurrent intent memories with learned persistence, soft interaction assignment, and a transition distribution predicting the next active intent; score candidates through a mixture of intent-specific predictions. Separate memory retention from current activation so sustained narrow preferences survive temporary switches, while individual actions can initiate legitimate new interests. This exact combination was not established by the retrieved papers. For causal next-item training, every state and routing decision must use only the observed prefix; temporal causality does not imply identified causal effects.
